mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last two months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS shows a sustained increase over the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within the last two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 1% within the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in the last month, it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of instances where UNRATE is above 8% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals strong demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% and GDPC1 grows > 2% YoY
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increases by more than 10% and GDPC1 grows by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within the last two months signal a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases and UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO shows a sustained decline and UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within the last two months.
